title: Polymer grating couplers
title_note: The paper reports "highly efficient grating couplers for polymer slab and strip waveguides fabricated by electron-beam lithography" (Waldhäusl et al., Appl. Opt. 1997, p.9383 abstract) and makes no "first" claim. Gratings with a blazed (asymmetric sawtooth) profile were written directly into the waveguide resist, replicated by embossing into an all-polymer chip, given a shorter period that leaves a single diffraction order (67 % input efficiency), graded in depth to shape the out-coupled beam, and curved to focus light into a strip waveguide (42 %). The plots are re-plotted from digitized points of Fig. 4, 5 and 7 and from the printed Tables 2-5; coupling angles and effective indices are not printed and appear only in hover as values derived for this story.
tagline: Electron-beam-written blazed gratings couple a light beam into polymer waveguides.

parts.name: quartz substrate
parts.role: Carries the resist film; lower index than the film.
parts.detail: A copolymer of PMMA "is spin coated onto a quartz substrate to yield a monomodal waveguide at a wavelength of 632.8 nm" (p.9383 col. 2). Table 1 gives the substrate index n_{s} = 1.457 at λ = 633 nm (p.9385). Plate size and thickness for this chip are not given; drawn as a plain slab stand-in.
parts.quote: A thin film consisting of a copolymer of PMMA of less than 1-µm thickness is spin coated onto a quartz substrate to yield a monomodal waveguide at a wavelength of 632.8 nm.

parts.name: PMMA-copolymer film
parts.role: Electron resist and waveguide layer in one.
parts.detail: "The electron resist used for the grating fabrication acts as both the resist material and the waveguide layer" (p.9383 col. 2), so the grating is written without a separate etch into the substrate (p.9383 col. 1). Table 1: film thickness t_{f} = 800 nm, film index n_{f} = 1.498, cover n_{c} = 1 (air), λ = 633 nm (p.9385). Film thickness and grating depth "allow only the coupling into the TE_{0} mode" (p.9384 col. 2). A slab-mode calculation with the Table 1 values (done for this story) gives one TE mode with effective index about 1.475, without the grating.

parts.name: electron beam
parts.role: Writes each period with a dose rising step by step.
parts.detail: Linear gratings are written with a variable-shaped-beam device (ZBA 23 Jenoptik). "Increasing the electron dose across every grating period stepwise from one edge of the period to the other can accomplish an asymmetric energy deposition. Over its whole grating length the pattern is drawn with a periodically repeating electron-dose distribution" (p.9383 col. 2 - p.9384 col. 1). Curved gratings use a second writer (LION LV 1 Jenoptik) in continuous path control mode, varying the dose by the table speed for "an asymmetric triangular energy deposition in every period" (p.9384 col. 1). Number of dose steps, dose values and beam energy are not given: the staircase is schematic.
parts.quote: Increasing the electron dose across every grating period stepwise from one edge of the period to the other can accomplish an asymmetric energy deposition.
parts.locator: Waldhäusl et al., Appl. Opt. 1997, p.9383 col. 2; p.9384 col. 1

geometry.dose_steps: schematic staircase rising across each 800 nm period; step count not stated

parts.name: input grating
parts.role: Blazed grating that couples the incident beam into the film.
parts.detail: Table 1 grating: period Λ = 800 nm, depth t_{g} = 250 nm, blazed profile, area 1 × 1 mm^{2} (p.9385). After development "the exposed regions of the resist are dissolved according to the varying electron dose, which results in blazed corrugated gratings"; the depth is set by the development time (p.9384 col. 1). The profile is not an ideal sawtooth: "During the exposure process a second inclination of an approximately 200 nm in base length is formed" (p.9385 col. 1); the close-up reads it as the steep side of the sawtooth (interpretation). A zero offset of about 80 nm is reported for the paper's e-beam gratings (Fig. 6, p.9387; Sec. 4-5); the close-up draws it under the Table 1 grating, with t_{g} taken as the peak-to-valley depth (assumed). No profile image with a scale is printed: the close-up draws the stated period, depth, 200 nm second inclination and 80 nm offset as straight facets; the facet orientation follows Fig. 1 (p.9384), where the input and output gratings are mirror images.
parts.quote: During the subsequent development process, the exposed regions of the resist are dissolved according to the varying electron dose, which results in blazed corrugated gratings.

parts.name: output grating
parts.role: Same grating 20 mm on; releases the guided light, mostly upward.
parts.detail: The chip "consists of an input and an output grating coupler with a 20-mm waveguide between" (p.9384 col. 1). The guided wave is coupled out "into different diffraction orders in the cover direction (I_{1}^{c} ... I_{n}^{c}) and in the substrate direction (I_{1}^{s} ... I_{n}^{s})" (p.9384 col. 2). Measured: output efficiency 95 %, about 65 % of the out-coupled light to the cover (blazing effect 65/35), leakage parameter 1.48 mm^{-1} (calculated 1.16 mm^{-1}) (p.9384 col. 2; p.9385 col. 1; Table 2). Facets mirror the input grating (Fig. 1).

parts.role: Incoming beam at the coupling angle onto the input grating.
parts.detail: The incoming beam I_{0} is partly reflected (I_{1}^{r} ... I_{n}^{r}) and transmitted (I_{1}^{t} ... parts.name: poly(α)-methylstyrene film
parts.role: Spin-coated over the embossed grating; the replica's waveguide.
parts.detail: "After cooling down, the waveguiding layer consisting of poly(α)-methylstyrene was spin coated on top of the embossed grating structure (Fig. 1). This material has a refractive index of n_{f} = 1.603 at a wavelength of λ = 633 nm. In an experiment we used a film layer of 450-nm thickness" (p.9384 col. 1). The grating now sits at the substrate-film interface, as Fig. 1 draws it. Replica results (Table 3, p.9385): input efficiency 46 %, output 75 %, about 74 % of the out-coupled light to the cover (Table 3 prints "74/36"), waveguide loss 1.2 dB/cm, throughput 12 %. "The measurements show that the replication of gratings into polymers does not affect the coupling efficiencies" (p.9385).

parts.name: single-order grating
parts.role: Fine rectangular grating; only one substrate order exists.
parts.detail: "In an experiment we realized a grating with a grating period of Λ = 250 nm and a corrugation depth of t_{g} = 150 nm. The grating profile is rectangular because the coupling efficiency does not depend on the grating profile" (p.9385 col. 2). Decreasing the period removes the higher orders; at best the guided light radiates "into only one diffraction order in only one direction (substrate, if n_{s} > n_{c})". Under the coupling condition the remaining light couples in "without diffraction into higher orders", comparable with a prism coupler. "The maximum achieved efficiency of this grating coupler has to be measured at 67%" (p.9385 col. 2). Fig. 3 draws the rectangular grating on the cover side of the waveguide. The film used for this experiment is not stated. With the Table 1 film (assumed, check for this story) Eq. (1) gives no air order and one substrate order, travelling backward against the guided wave, as Fig. 3 draws it.
parts.quote: The maximum achieved efficiency of this grating coupler has to be measured at 67%.

parts.name: variable-depth grating
parts.role: Blazed grating whose groove depth changes along its 2 mm.
parts.detail: Designed so that the out-coupled field is Gaussian, peaking at half the grating length and falling to 1/e at both ends (Eq. (3)-(7), p.9386): this fixes the leakage parameter α(z) (Fig. 4) and, through the Tamir-Peng formalism, the depth t_{g}(z) (Fig. 5, solid). "The grating with a length of 2 mm was split into 25 subareas of 80-µm length", each written with its own dose, so "each period of the grating remained a sawtooth, but the groove depth varied over the grating length" (p.9386 col. 2 - p.9387 col. 1). Depths measured with a secondary electron microscope (Fig. 5, squares) agree with the design "except for a difference of approximately 80 nm caused by the zero offset" (p.9387 col. 1). Other parameters as Table 1. Periods are drawn far wider than to scale.
parts.quote: Thus each period of the grating remained a sawtooth, but the groove depth varied over the grating length, resulting in the required corrugation depths.

parts.name: focusing gratings
parts.role: Curved blazed lines; the first focuses into the film, the second recollimates.
parts.detail: Curved lines from Eq. (9) are ellipses with one common focal point (Eq. (11), p.9387-9388); a correction term for the 5 × 10^{-3} effective-index step at the zero offset (Eq. (13), (14)) reduces aberration (p.9388 col. 1). Written with the LION LV 1 (fine beam, so the pattern area is reduced); blazed; Table 1 parameters; focal length f = 4 mm (p.9388). parts.name: strip waveguide
parts.role: Ridge between two dissolved bands; receives the focused light.
parts.detail: Strip waveguides are written directly: "at their right and left borders rectangular areas are exposed with a high electron dose. During the development process the resist of these areas is completely dissolved. Thus ridge waveguide structures are fabricated. The chosen width of 20 µm guarantees a strong decay of the evanescent field inside the rectangular areas" (p.9384 col. 1). The focusing chip: strip width 15 µm, length 2 mm, gratings with their focal points at its two ends (p.9389 col. 1, Fig. 9). Strips 10 µm and 5 µm wide gave throughputs below about 3 % and 1 % (p.9389 col. 2). Width drawn enlarged in the plan view.

chapters.line: A quartz plate to carry a polymer waveguide.
chapters.action: plain quartz slab slides in (chip side view, no scale)

chapters.line: One PMMA copolymer film serves as resist and light guide.
chapters.action: the PMMA-copolymer film spreads over the slab (spin coating); a thin metal layer settles on top

chapters.line: The dose rises step by step across every period.
chapters.action: zoom into a true-scale close-up of four periods (nm); shaped-beam shots, five per period (schematic), dose rising across each period; exposed resist tinted by dose; metal layer on top

chapters.line: Development dissolves resist by dose, leaving asymmetric grooves.
chapters.action: metal layer gone (removal not described, said in hover); resist dissolves deepest where the dose was highest: long facet about 600 nm, steep side about 200 nm, depth 250 nm, grating region about 80 nm below the surface

chapters.line: One grating feeds the guided mode; a second releases it.
chapters.action: chip side view after Fig. 2 (20 mm compressed, break mark); beam and orders at the Fig. 2 angles (derived values in hover); guided glow with 0.6 dB/cm loss and exp(-2 alpha z) decay under the output grating; cover orders brighter (65 %)

chapters.line: A nickel master embosses PMMA; a spin-coated film guides the light.
chapters.action: Fig. 1 sequence: nickel and copper grow on the chip, the master lifts off, a heated PMMA plate comes in, the master presses and lifts, the PaMS film spreads over the embossed plate; light in and out, cover orders about 74 %

chapters.line: Fed from below, a finer grating allows one diffraction order.
chapters.action: Fig. 3 view: rectangular 250 nm grating on top of the film on a SiO2 plate; beam through prism and liquid at the drawn angle; guided wave runs back to the left; faint uncoupled light

chapters.line: Groove depth changes along the grating to shape the beam.
chapters.action: model left: 2 mm grating in 25 subareas; each subarea takes the Fig. 5 measured depth as the pen reaches it; dashed design depth follows the calculated pen; alternate Fig. 4 moves a marker

chapters.line: The out-coupled light peaks near the middle of the grating.
chapters.action: model left: guided light enters the graded grating from its start; out-coupled light up to the pen with brightness from the Fig. 7 trace

chapters.line: Curved lines focus the light into a narrow strip.
chapters.action: isometric plan after Fig. 9: strip between dissolved bands, Eq. (11) ellipse-shaped lines 4 mm from each strip end (lengths in true ratio, widths enlarged); input upper right, converging fan, strip, diverging fan, output up-left

chapters.line: Measured coupling into the waveguide, grating by grating.
chapters.action: model left: focusing chip lit; plot right: input efficiencies by coupler (alternate: master vs replica chip tables)
